question: A patient with aspirin-exacerbated asthma and co-existing allergic rhinitis needs add-on therapy. Which leukotriene modifier is most appropriate for this patient?

answers.text: Zileuton — it inhibits 5-LOX, preventing all leukotriene synthesis upstream

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Zileuton does inhibit 5-LOX at the synthesis level, but it carries hepatotoxicity risk requiring regular liver function monitoring and is less commonly used in practice. Crucially, it is not approved for allergic rhinitis — making it suboptimal for this patient's dual condition.

answers.text: Montelukast — it blocks CysLT1 receptors and is also approved for allergic rhinitis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In aspirin-exacerbated asthma, COX inhibition shunts arachidonic acid toward the 5-LOX pathway, producing excess cysteinyl leukotrienes. Montelukast blocks their downstream bronchospastic effects at CysLT1 receptors. Its additional approval for allergic rhinitis makes it uniquely suited to address both conditions simultaneously.

answers.text: Both agents are equally effective because they block the same final pathway

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: They act at different points: zileuton inhibits leukotriene synthesis (5-LOX enzyme), while montelukast blocks the CysLT1 receptor downstream. Their efficacy, safety profiles, and approved indications differ — montelukast is preferred here because it covers rhinitis and has a better safety profile.

answers.text: Neither — leukotriene modifiers are ineffective in aspirin-exacerbated asthma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Leukotriene modifiers are particularly effective in aspirin-exacerbated asthma precisely because excess cysteinyl leukotrienes drive the pathogenesis. When COX is inhibited by aspirin, arachidonic acid is diverted to the 5-LOX pathway — making leukotriene blockade a targeted intervention.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the leukotriene modifier section. Montelukast blocks CysLT1 receptors (downstream); zileuton inhibits 5-LOX (upstream). Montelukast is preferred in aspirin-exacerbated asthma with rhinitis because of its dual indication and better safety profile.

Excellent reasoning. The key distinction for exams: montelukast/zafirlukast = CysLT1 receptor antagonists; zileuton = 5-LOX synthesis inhibitor. Montelukast's dual indication for asthma and rhinitis makes it the single best agent for patients with both conditions.
